title: Grateful Dead Live at Curtis Hixon Convention Hall on 1973-12-18
lineage: SBD Reel master > cassette > DAT > CDR (unknown gens) > EAC > CDWav retracking> SHN

ai_review.summary: Crisp soundboard capture of a smoking ’73 Hamilton show – epic Dark Star, soaring Eyes of the World, and stellar vocals make it a standout recording.
ai_review.review: The soundboard source delivers clear, well‑balanced audio with only minor glitches, letting listeners fully enjoy one of the band’s most inspired 1973 performances. Highlights include an unforgettable Dark Star, a blazing Eyes of the World (with the Spanish Jam), and a heartfelt rendition of Greatest Story Ever Told, all driven by tight playing and Jerry Garcia’s soaring vocals.

ai_rating.rationale: Average star rating ≈4.46 across 13 reviews; overwhelmingly positive comments on both musical performance and recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Generally crisp and well‑balanced; a few minor audio mess‑ups noted but nothing that detracts from overall clarity.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
poor_songs: First‑set selections (generally not the best versions)
Weather Report Suite Parts I & II
show_quality.setlist_flow: Strong second set with seamless segues (China/Rider, Dark Star into Eyes) and a high‑energy climax; first set solid but less remarkable.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s vocals praised as beautiful on Wharf Rat and powerful throughout Dark Star; guitar work noted as “slashing” and tight.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir described as slashing, playing very well and delivering psychedelic storytelling between songs.
band_member_comments.Drums: Billy Kreutzmann’s solo highlighted, propelling the band into Eyes of the World.
